system.name: Xkernel
system.one_liner: a system that enables principled, in-situ performance tuning of any tunable constant directly on a deployed Linux kernel via Scoped Indirect Execution

components.name: Kernel Source Code
components.role: annotated source input, marked with <line, token> locations of tunable constants

components.name: Kernel Binary
components.role: compiled kernel binary analyzed offline together with the source to build the scope table

components.name: Scope Table
components.role: global table of tunable constants with columns ConstID, Val, Expression, CS, SS, Status, built by one-time offline static analysis

components.name: Xk-stub
components.role: generated stub header for a given ConstID, created via xk-gen

components.name: Xk-tune
components.role: user-authored tuning program combining the stub with a policy

components.name: Kernel Binary
components.role: running kernel binary in kernel space, containing the critical-span (CS)-marked code region to be tuned

components.name: Instructions (Policy & SetVal)
components.role: synthesized indirection instructions that apply the policy and set the tuned value

components.name: XK-runtime
components.role: runtime component that attaches the instructions and transitions the kernel from the original value to the new one safely

flows.what: offline static analysis of symbolic state expressions, critical span (CS), and safe span (SS)
attach and safe transition to the new value

content.key_idea: Xkernel performs one-time offline static analysis to derive a global Scope Table of tunable constants' critical and safe spans, then lets a user-space tuning program synthesize indirection instructions that XK-runtime attaches into the running kernel via Kprobe redirection.
content.reading_order: Left to right and top to bottom: a user annotates kernel source, offline processing builds the Scope Table, then user-space steps (Xk-stub, Xk-tune) flow down across the user/kernel-space divide into synthesized instructions attached by XK-runtime.

summary: This figure gives the system overview of Xkernel, which provides principled, in-situ performance tunability for OS kernels via a technique called Scoped Indirect Execution. A user annotates kernel source-code locations (<line, token>) that, together with the kernel binary, are offline-processed into a Scope Table listing each tunable constant's ID, value, expression, critical span (CS), safe span (SS), and status; this one-time offline analysis only needs updating when the kernel is redeployed. In user space, the user generates an Xk-stub via 'xk-gen', combines it with a policy to form Xk-tune, and loads it ('xk-load') into the system. The Scope Table's CS/SS entries are used to synthesize indirection instructions (Policy & SetVal) wired to the live kernel binary via Kprobe redirection, which XK-runtime then attaches and safely transitions into execution. The diagram is a flat, mixed-corner box diagram split by a horizontal user-space/kernel-space divider, using color-coded bands traced consistently between the table and the kernel binary, with command-line snippets annotated directly on the flow arrows.
summary_zh: 该图展示 Xkernel 系统概览：用户标注内核源码后，与内核二进制一起离线生成作用域表（含 ConstID、CS、SS 等列，一次性离线分析）；用户态通过 xk-gen/xk-stub 与策略组合成 Xk-tune 并加载进内核态，利用 Kprobe 重定向与作用域表合成间接指令，由 XK-runtime 挂载并安全切换生效。
